# `get_lock_position`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Report the stored guide-star lock position.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | PURE GETTER / established (64-bit build; 32-bit build matches (READ)) |
| Side-effect tier | A |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0x78520 (64-bit guider build) |

Params are not read. The result is a two-element array [x, y] in pixels when the stored lock-validity byte is set, and JSON null when it is not. A missing guide object is reported as error 300. Beyond that stored flag there is no guarantee the position is current.

Side effects: Copies the stored lock position only.

Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). ## Example

Request, request:

```json
{"id":21,"method":"get_lock_position"}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_lock_position","result":[10.5,20.25],"code":0,"id":22}
```

Reply, error:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_lock_position","error":"internal error","code":300,"id":23}
```
